p: Lakeside was built in an old chalk quarry, which is why the area around it has those dramatic cliffs and lakes. The quarrying past is also behind one of the most unexpected nature spots in Essex: Chafford Gorges Nature Park, near Chafford Hundred, where old chalk pits have become wild, steep-sided gorges with lakes, wildlife and walking trails. It's a cracking place to blow away the cobwebs.

Thurrock has real history along its riverbank too. Tilbury Fort, looked after by English Heritage, is an impressive star-shaped fort that guarded the Thames for centuries. A little further downstream, Coalhouse Fort at East Tilbury is a Victorian fort with open days and riverside walks.

For birdwatchers and nature lovers, RSPB Rainham Marshes, just over the border near Purfleet, is a big wetland reserve with boardwalks, hides and a visitor centre. It's very family-friendly, with easy paths and loads of wildlife to spot.
If you're visiting with smaller children, the main Lakeside Shopping Centre is packed with places to eat and shops, and the boardwalk area around the lake is pleasant for a quick wander.

Grays itself has a small town centre and a long connection with the river. On a fine day, the Thames views from the riverside paths are worth a look, with big ships making their way to and from the docks.
Being so close to the M25, this is an easy trip for families across Essex, Kent and east London, but weekends and holidays can be busy, so plan your arrival for a calmer start.
